issues.title: Embedded agency, continual skill evolution, and the mechanics of test-time reasoning
issues.blurb: Fresh results probe how foundation-model agents cooperate via similarity inference, consolidate experience into transferable skills, and allocate inference compute, alongside formal treatments of causality, ablation, and pretraining inductive biases.

issues.title: Agent memory continuity, failure detection, and rigorous evaluation of long-horizon reasoning
issues.blurb: Recent work advances persistent state and hierarchical memory for agents and sequence models, develops efficient monitors and detectors for mid-run failures and cross-session misuse, and exposes how answer-only scoring inflates claims of scientific reasoning while formal synthesis and test-time latent optimization offer more reliable paths forward.

issues.title: Agent memory architectures, multi-objective control, and the fragility of alignment
issues.blurb: This issue gathers recent work on structured and evolving memory for long-horizon agents, policy-space methods for multi-reward optimization, and formal analyses of value fragility, imitation, and transformer expressivity under transcript management. The through-line is how agents can maintain competence and controllability over extended interactions without collapsing under conflicting objectives or imperfect proxies.

issues.title: Self-improvement loops, internal signals, and agent reliability
issues.blurb: Recent work probes how models can govern their own memory and compute, train via outcome-verified self-distillation or meta-evolution, and whether self-verification, belief simulation, or introspection actually track ground truth. The selections emphasize rigorous controls on test-time methods, transaction-safe agent state, and hard evaluations of agents in realistic settings.

issues.title: Residual routing, capability nucleation, and agent self-diagnosis
issues.blurb: Today's papers probe how information and capabilities actually form and fail inside models and agents: multi-head residual streams and driven-nucleation kinetics for emergence, training-free divergence routing and action-centric graphs for inference-time fusion and memory, plus rigorous diagnoses of asymmetric safety collapse under merging, quantization damage masked by error budgets, and learnable blind-spot diagnosis that lets agents improve without weight updates.

issues.title: Selective belief, fragile oracles, and calibrated agent reliability
issues.blurb: Recent work tightens the foundations of how models revise beliefs under partial credibility, quantifies over-trust in derived signals and mis-scoring by agent benchmarks, and pairs these diagnostics with concrete advances in certified solvers, graph-aware retrieval, end-to-end operational policies, and efficient world-action models.

issues.title: Agent frontiers under audit: open-ended research, multi-agent coordination, and non-composing evaluations
issues.blurb: This issue gathers rigorous new work testing the real capabilities and failure modes of LLM agents, from shadow evaluations of open-ended AI R&D automation and long-horizon clinical/office workflows, through causal audits of latent multi-agent communication and objective misalignment, to organizational designs for multi-agent systems and epistemic limits on composing benchmark inferences.

items.title: A game theory for foundation models shows new paths to rational cooperation through similarity inference
items.authors: Alexander Meulemans, Maciej Wołczyk, Marissa A. Weis, Rajai Nasser, Roberta Rocca, Seijin Kobayashi, Guillaume Lajoie, Angelika Steger, Blake Richards, Marcus Hutter, James Manyika, Rif A. Saurous, João Sacramento, Blaise Agüera y Arcas
items.summary: Foundation model agents in social dilemmas converge to stable cooperation under optimal planning, contradicting classical Nash predictions of mutual defection. The authors introduce the embedded Bayesian agent, which maintains uncertainty about its own decision algorithms and treats its deliberation as evidence of similarity to partners, formalizing an embedded equilibrium as a new solution concept.

items.title: ReflectRL: Learning from Golden Negative Trajectories via Reflective-to-Direct Reasoning
items.authors: Jinhe Bi, Chennan Zhou, Zengjie Jin, Aniri, Shuo Lu, Wenke Huang, Hu Cao, Xun Xiao, Zhihong Zhu, Volker Tresp, Fei Shen, Yunpu Ma, Tat-Seng Chua
items.summary: Failed expert trajectories, previously discarded, provide valuable signals when treated as objects of reflection rather than imitation. ReflectRL elicits reflective reasoning from these golden negatives then transitions the policy to direct reasoning, consistently improving on-policy training across nine benchmarks and multiple backbones with low overhead.

items.title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
items.authors: Mohsen Hariri, Weicong Chen, Nahal Shahini, Vikash Singh, Kai Ye, Amirhossein Samandar, Debargha Ganguly, Sreehari Sankar, Yanyan Zhang, Shouren Wang, Jerry Peng, Biyao Zhang, Michael Hinczewski, Vipin Chaudhary
items.summary: The paper formalizes test-time scaling as budgeted inference over the autoregressive prefix tree and distinguishes single-trajectory, leaf-level, and prefix-level regimes. It supplies evaluation profiles that separate system performance from candidate diagnostics, protocol-matched compute reporting, and reproducibility requirements, releasing over two billion reasoning traces.

items.title: Logic Before Language: Pre-pretraining on Formal Derivations Fosters Skill Acquisition and Compressibility
items.authors: Jo-Ku Cheng, Nikolaos Aletras, Marco Valentino
items.summary: Pre-pretraining on formal logical derivations accelerates linguistic skill acquisition, reaching 80 percent accuracy with 36 billion fewer tokens than standard initialization at 100B-token scale. The resulting lower-rank, spectrally concentrated representations also enable pruning to roughly 33 percent sparsity while matching dense baseline performance.

items.title: Cross-Model KV Cache Transfer in LLM Families: A Closed-Form Linear Mapping for Prefill Reuse
items.authors: Taekyung Heo, Rasoul Shafipour, Ritchie Zhao, Maximilian Golub, Mohammad Mahdi Kamani, Ritika Borkar, Makesh Tarun Chandran, Pantea Zardoshti, Bita Darvish Rouhani
items.summary: A closed-form ridge regression mapper transfers KV caches across same-family models that share head dimensions, stripping RoPE for position-free reuse. It retains 73-98 percent of standalone-prefill accuracy on multiple pairs while running 2.7-25x faster than re-prefill and remaining stable across multi-turn handoffs.

items.title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
items.authors: Shuhan Xue, Zixin Ding, Yichen Shen, Yinjie Wang, Zhenfei Yin, Yingcheng Wu, Yuxin Chen, Mengdi Wang, Ling Yang
items.summary: PAST-Bench isolates whether retained experience (preferences, histories, skills) produces later-task gains via the intended save-retrieve-update pathway across 26 scenarios. Gains exist but are uneven; Hermes+ interventions raise average improvement and pathway evidence, especially on state-update tasks, though results remain model- and capability-dependent.

items.title: ContinualSkillBench: Can LLM Agents Truly Evolve Their Capabilities?
items.authors: Tianyi Guan, Yiding Wang, Haotong Yang, Siyuan Cao, Shirui Liu, Yi Hu, Jiaqi Li, Muhan Zhang
items.summary: The benchmark evaluates in-context continual skill learning across five domains of interconnected subtasks ordered by difficulty. Sequential execution improves performance, yet much of the gain arises from context adaptation rather than reusable skill abstraction; explicit skills help selectively while weaker models accumulate fragmented task-specific collections.

items.title: Computing Actual Causes for Neural Network Predictions under Structured Causal Inputs
items.authors: Jannick Strobel, Muqsit Azeem, Stefan Leue
items.summary: Explanations are formalized as Halpern-Pearl actual causes under Boolean SCMs that capture input dependencies, computed via bound propagation and branch-and-bound with completeness and minimality guarantees. The method scales to search spaces of 10^13 candidates and shows that ignoring dependencies produces 14.9 percent spurious causes.

items.title: Sensitivity, Causality, and Repair Dissociate: A Layer-Wise Analysis of Perturbation Robustness and Its Scaling
items.authors: Nathan Labiosa, David Buff, Ena Nayak, Erica Donno
items.summary: Layer maps for representational sensitivity, causal recovery via activation restoration, and adapter repair capacity dissociate under surface perturbations, with anti-correlation between sensitivity and causality. Two propagation regimes appear, late-accumulation strengthens with scale, and cascade disruption explains why causally flagged early layers are often the worst adapter sites.

items.title: A Theory of Conditional Collapse under Low-Rank Weight-Space Ablations: I. The Single-Block Theory and Synthetic Validation
items.authors: Abdallah Khemais
items.summary: Exact results characterize when weight-space ablation of residual carriers collapses conditional computation, contrasting the effects of patching (contrast) versus ablation (absolute level). An attention-head interaction formula is derived with second-order remainder, and synthetic transformers confirm the predictions with strong rank correlation to measured interactions.

items.title: AtumAI: A Principled Framework for Agentic Generation of Datacenter Control-Plane Policies
items.authors: Qiushi Lin, Chaojie Zhang, Íñigo Goiri, Aditya Akella, Ricardo Bianchini, Jovan Stojkovic
items.summary: AtumAI compiles plain-language goals into formal, machine-checkable specifications of objectives, constraints, and evaluation, then searches the space with a diffusion model, evolutionary algorithm, and surrogate. Across workload placement, resource scaling, and power management, the generated policies outperform expert-engineered baselines while reducing task onboarding from months of engineering to a description. The framework makes agentic search formal, transferable across tasks, and systematically broader than pure LLM proposal.

items.title: Magnet: Detecting Cross-Session AI Misuse Through Capability Accumulation
items.authors: Natalie Isak, Matthew Dressman
items.summary: Attackers can decompose harmful goals into innocuous units executed across isolated agent sessions, accumulating composable capabilities that single-session detectors miss. Magnet aggregates capability evidence at the user level across time, attracting relevant artifacts into a compact bundle for detection rather than inspecting sessions individually. It demonstrates that cross-session decomposition can elicit more harmful capability than equivalent single-session attacks and provides an efficient correlator-based countermeasure.

items.title: Optimizing Minimax Regret in Uncertain MDPs with Small Sets of Policies
items.authors: Sterre Lutz, Daniël Vos, Matthijs T.J. Spaan, Anna Lukina
items.summary: When model uncertainty is resolved just before execution, a small set of k policies prepared in advance can be selected to minimize maximax regret over a set of MDPs. The problem is NP-hard; KAPS solves it exactly via nested branch-and-bound that jointly partitions MDPs and optimizes the shared policies. The largest regret reductions occur when moving from one to two policies, and in the single-policy case KAPS matches or exceeds prior methods while proving optimality more often.

items.title: Abduction Without a Body? Representational Grounding and the Abduction Loop for Scientific Hypothesis Generation
items.authors: Michael Farmer
items.summary: Online embodiment is unnecessary for identity abduction, the inference that two structures are the same object under an explicit correspondence reached via representational transformations that expose latent invariants. The Abduction Loop generates representations, extracts motifs, canonicalizes them in convention space, retrieves across domains, forms identity hypotheses, and adversarially verifies them, with abstention as default. A documented multimodal episode equating a gravitational-memory complex with the Kaiser-Squires operator motivates the architecture and a falsifiable DAB-30 benchmark.

items.title: Real-Time Detection and Repair of LLM Agent Failures
items.authors: Sunny Dubey
items.summary: A one-class echo-state-network ensemble with CUSUM alarms detects 71 percent of failures from step telemetry alone at a 5 percent false-alarm budget (AUROC 0.872), with advantage growing over longer post-onset horizons. Deterministic verification of stated totals against actual tool results catches 60-96 percent of failures at zero false positives on healthy runs and transfers without retraining. Closing the loop by rolling back and re-running flagged trajectories recovers 45 percent of failures and lifts task success from 52 percent to 73 percent at roughly one extra model call.

items.title: Right Answer, Wrong Method: Shortcut Hacking Misleads the Evaluation of LLM Reasoning on Frontier Science Benchmarks
items.authors: Xuan Ren, Weiqi Zhai, Tianle Pu, Yihua Zhu, Hu Wei, Bing Zhao
items.summary: Solution hacking occurs when models reach correct answers via numerical search, enumeration, guessing, or answer-first verification instead of valid task-targeted derivation. The rate rises sharply with difficulty (2.2 percent on common problems to 37.4 percent on HLE) and accounts for 8-44 percent of credited correct answers across frontier models. Anti-hacking judges and instructions substantially lower reported accuracy while affecting genuine correct solutions far less, showing answer-only metrics overestimate scientific reasoning.

items.title: Mamba with Hierarchical Memory: Solving Representation Bottleneck in Long Sequence Modeling
items.authors: Qinwen Wang, Jieping Luo, Aoxiang Qin, Ruoyu Zhao, Jianxiong Tang, Wei Zhang, Zhichao Lu, Luziwei Leng
items.summary: HMM adds a lightweight working memory that extracts slow paragraph-level semantics from Mamba's fast sensory states and compresses them into persistent long-term memory for retrieval. The hierarchy overcomes the fixed-state bottleneck of recurrent linear attention models and yields cross-task generalization via parametric learning. On Passkey Retrieval and LongBench-E it improves success by 34-37 percent and reasoning accuracy by 1.6-14 percent over strong Mamba baselines while adding only 2 percent parameters.

items.title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
items.authors: Zhaoxin Yu, Qi Shen, Hengli Li, Zhaowei Zhang, Song-Chun Zhu, Chi Zhang, Zilong Zheng
items.summary: GradCuit inserts optimizable latent states at a chosen Transformer layer so that causal attention supplies differentiable paths from every continuation-token log-probability back to the latents, enabling direct reward-weighted credit assignment. Across five backbones and three benchmarks it reaches 64.5 percent average accuracy, beating chain-of-thought by 6.6 points and the strongest prior method by 2.4 points, with lower variance across learning rates. Gradient attribution concentrates on reasoning-connector tokens and early-to-middle layers prove most effective.

items.title: LiveMem: Maintaining Memory State Continuity in Long-Running LLM Inference
items.authors: Zhichen Liu, Ruihan Sun, Hengjie Yang, Zipeng Wu, Zhaohan Chen, Xiaofan Zhang, Yang Xu
items.summary: LiveMem augments a full-attention LLM with a fixed-capacity memory state whose lifetime is independent of the active KV window, preserving historical information across context turnovers. Memory-oriented post-training and state-aware serving make the state load-bearing after originating tokens are released. On LongMemEval it answers questions from the memory state alone even after evidence is removed from context, establishing state continuity as a complementary abstraction for continual inference.

items.title: MechGeo: Autoformalizing and Proving Euclidean Geometry in Lean 4
items.authors: Hao Shen, Junyu Guo, Tian Cui, Yuxuan Xiao, Lihong Zhi
items.summary: MechGeo uses GeoFormalizer to translate informal geometry into Lean via an intermediate representation with iterative structural and semantic repair, then GeoProver plans proofs, derives lemmas, and algebraizes subgoals whose certificates are kernel-checked. On 43 historical IMO geometry problems it proves 29 statements outright and, for the rest, produces Lean-verified counterexamples plus repaired proofs. It also proves 12 of 14 LEAP Lean-IMO-Bench geometry statements for the first time and refutes the remaining two.

items.title: Fragility of Value under Imperfect Alignment
items.authors: Winter Cross
items.summary: The paper formalizes idealized alignment training that enforces a proxy condition on an agent's value function before world-optimization. It derives conditions on the human value function and proxy accuracy under which an η-catastrophic value function (one that drives expected human value below η under unbounded optimization) is still deployed, highlighting over-optimization risk and motivating designs such as quantilizers that limit optimization pressure rather than relying solely on pre-deployment training.

items.title: Transcript-Managed Transformers: Monotone Multi-Agent Collapse and Universality with Two Pop-Enabled Transcripts
items.authors: Sergey Salishev
items.summary: The work models fixed-precision causal Transformers that manage transcripts partitioned into bounded channels, with stay/push/pop operations. It proves that pop-free (append-only) systems realize exactly deterministic finite-state transductions even for multi-agent monotone protocols, while two pop-enabled channels restore stack discipline and yield universality (RE), with exact simulation costs and invariance results under fixed block size and visibility.

items.title: The Grokked Illusion: True Equilibrium Mitigates Catastrophic Forgetting
items.authors: Xiaotian Zhang, Lai Shun Chan, Yue Shang, Entao Yang, Ge Zhang
items.summary: Using modular arithmetic grokking, the authors compare AdamW-trained transformers against high-entropy models sampled via Wang-Landau molecular dynamics that achieve identical saturated performance. After forcing both to memorize random-label data, AdamW models drop original-task accuracy below 75% while high-entropy models retain ~95%, linked to higher effective rank in attention and MLP weights that buffers against interference; perfect generalization therefore masks differences in robustness.

items.title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
items.authors: Luca Viano, Antoine Moulin, Audrey Huang, Volkan Cevher, Philip Amortila, Dylan J. Foster
items.summary: The paper shows that interactive expert queries along the learner's trajectories relax representational requirements: realizability of the expert's value function (rather than its full policy) suffices for statistical efficiency. It introduces OVI, an on-policy interactive algorithm that is computationally efficient given a linear maximization oracle, proves a matching negative result that offline methods require policy-class complexity under weaker assumptions, and demonstrates largest gains when the learner is less expressive than the expert.

items.title: Don't Mix Rewards, Mix Policies: Policy Decomposition and Optimization for Multi-Reward RL
items.authors: Ruiming Liang, Yi Zhong, Yizhen Yuan, Yinan Zheng, Tianyi Tan, Tianyue Wang, Haiyun Guo, Jinqiao Wang, Xianyuan Zhan
items.summary: PRISM decomposes multi-reward RL into standalone positive policies plus a global negative policy instead of mixing reward signals, thereby reducing alignment-tax conflicts during optimization. The resulting policies can be flexibly composed at inference for controllable trade-offs; experiments on scientific reasoning, tool-use, and helpfulness-safety show consistent gains over multi-reward baselines together with explicit preference control.

items.title: LEMUR: Learning to Align with Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning from Preference Feedback
items.authors: Manith Adikari, Bei Peng, Samuele Vinanzi, Angelo Cangelosi
items.summary: LEMUR bridges multi-objective RL and preference-based RL by jointly learning policies and multiple objective-specific reward models from interactive multi-human preference feedback, without requiring pre-specified scalar or vector rewards. The framework enables agents to balance competing objectives during learning and outperforms baselines on standard multi-objective benchmarks.

items.title: Beyond Retrieval: Analytic Memory for Multimodal Agents
items.authors: Zhoujin Tian, Yao Tian, Hao Zhang, Cheng Chen, Yakun Li, Lei Zhang, Xiaofang Zhou
items.summary: AdaMM treats analytic memory as a complement to retrieval memory: it extracts provenance-linked attribute-value observations from dialogue, images and metadata, discovers recurring field structures, and materializes them for filtering, aggregation, ranking and temporal comparison. A memory-aware planner decomposes queries into retrieval versus analytic operations; gains reach 11.3% and 7.3% on MemEye and MemGallery long-term multimodal benchmarks.

items.title: Self-Play Meets Skill Evolution: Self-Evolving Search Agents that Pose, Solve, and Remember
items.authors: Zenghuang Fu, Zhaoyang Li, Qiuyuan Ai, Haoyu Wu, Minghui Wu, Chenxu Zhao, Ante Wang, Guannan He, Changwei Wang
items.summary: SESA couples a challenger that poses problems with a solver that retrieves from an evolving skill memory; informative failures are distilled into reusable skills that rewrite the memory, altering both solver behavior and the future problem distribution. Skills shape on-policy trajectories so benefits enter parameters as well as the external bank, yielding 1.2–3.2 point gains over self-play baselines across seven QA benchmarks while retaining optional inference-time retrieval.

items.title: Zero-Mem: Zero-Token Memory Operations for LLM Agents
items.authors: Yilin Xiao, Zhehan Zhu, Yujing Zhang, Jin Chen, Zijin Hong, Luyao Zhuang, Qinggang Zhang, Shengyuan Chen, Xiaocao Ouyang, Lingfei Ren, Xiao Huang
items.summary: Zero-Mem performs all memory operations without any intermediate LLM calls or token consumption outside final QA: original traces are organized into an entity-context graph and a temporal hierarchy; queries weigh and retrieve from both views, with deterministic calibration to discard conflicts and ground answers. It matches competitive long-memory QA performance while cutting memory-operation time by 57.6% relative to the fastest baseline under identical final-reader budgets.

items.title: CAGE: Certified Authorization under Typed-Return Uncertainty for Tool-Using Agents
items.authors: Blaise Delattre, Cong Wang, Yang Cao
items.summary: CAGE certifies that a candidate tool action remains authorized over a joint neighborhood of plausible correctly-bound returns (one admissible binding fault plus bounded numerical drift), proving that separate categorical and numerical certificates do not compose. It enumerates discrete branches exactly and certifies continuous perturbations within each, eliminating in-budget false allows that pointwise gates admit while preserving useful autonomy across synthetic, policy-as-code, regulatory and real-transaction settings.

items.title: Sample More, Reflect Less: Self-Refine and Reflexion Lose to Repeated Sampling at Equal Token Cost, from 1.5B to 7B
items.authors: Iliya Mirzaei
items.summary: A controlled experiment across 1.5B–7B models and two math benchmarks shows that self-refine, Reflexion, and other self-inspection methods are never reliably better than equal-token repeated sampling (majority vote), and are often significantly worse. Self-inspection comparisons are uniformly negative; as models scale, Best-of-N selection hurts less while rewriting continues to lag. The work releases full generations and verification scripts, underscoring that extra tokens, not the reflective mechanism, drive most gains.

items.title: Frontis-MA1: Training an AI4AI Model towards Recursive Self-Improvement in Machine Learning Engineering
items.authors: Junlin Yang, Che Jiang, Yu Fu, et al.
items.summary: The authors release OpenMLE, a full-stack environment for RSI research in ML engineering (gym, RL operators, evolutionary search), and post-train Frontis-MA1 (35B) around four atomic program-evolution operators. On MLE-Bench Lite the system raises medal average from 39% to 61–71% under tight GPU budgets, approaching or matching frontier closed models, with transfer to held-out NatureBench. Learning and long-horizon evolution are coupled in one loop with open weights and code.

items.title: Stage-Replay Divergence Follows the KV Cache: Fixed-Prefix Precision Controls and Bidirectional Cache Transplantation
items.authors: Alexander Boesgaard Lorup
items.summary: Exact-token stage replay of reasoning prefixes produces divergent suffixes and correctness labels under BF16 even when token sequences match, while FP32 eliminates decoded disagreement. Bidirectional transplantation of the full K/V cache makes every divergent continuation follow its donor cache, establishing the boundary KV state as a causally sufficient carrier of trajectory divergence. The results show that numerical precision and live-cache fidelity, not just token identity, govern replay reliability.

items.title: LLMs struggle to simulate human belief updates in controlled environments
items.authors: Sebastian Pohl, Harsh Mehta, Pranav Mambayil, et al.
items.summary: Six LLMs conditioned on real participant personas are compared 1-to-1 against 391 humans who updated stances after reading Reddit comments. Models can match post-update distributions only when given true initial stances; they fail to generate realistic initials or faithful updates from self-generated ones, exhibiting systematic over-neutrality, smaller shifts, and poor ranking of comment persuasiveness. Demographic/personality personas add little, limiting reliability of multi-round social simulations.

items.title: MemTxn: A Transaction Boundary for Source-Supported Updates and Complete-State Recovery in Agent Memory
items.authors: Hanshuai Cui, Zhiqing Tang, Zhi Yao, et al.
items.summary: MemTxn adds an external governance layer that verifies source support for memory writes, resolves conflicting versions temporally, and restores complete application-visible state after faults via a durable snapshot journal. It perfectly accepts supported originals and rejects hard negatives on an audit set, restores full multi-key state under persistent faults, and lifts FactConsolidation F1 by large margins across answer models. The design treats memory updates as transactional rather than best-effort.

items.title: Meta-Task: Turning Terminal Task Synthesis into a Terminal Task for Scalable Agent Training
items.authors: Zhihong Pan, Jiyuan He, Kai Zhang, et al.
items.summary: Task synthesis itself is cast as a Terminal-Bench-style agent problem executed inside a real container, so generated tasks are executed and verified in-loop for consistency and executability. Multi-phase specification design plus optional external materials increase diversity; LLM-as-judge filtering yields high-quality trajectories. Fine-tuning on only ~3k such trajectories substantially lifts Qwen3 models on Terminal-Bench 2.0, outperforming concurrent methods with less data.

items.title: Not All Tokens Deserve Equal Credit: Counterfactual Sensitivity Credit Reallocation for Long-CoT Reasoning
items.authors: Qiangqiang He, Zhongheng Wu, ZiJian Wang
items.summary: Counterfactual re-scoring of fixed trajectories under opposing outcome claims reveals that most tokens shift likelihood in the same direction regardless of asserted correctness, and large shifts concentrate on substitutable surface tokens rather than core reasoning content. Privileged self-teacher signals therefore supply unreliable answer-aligned directions. CSCR extends GRPO by down-weighting highly sensitive tokens and renormalizing advantages, consistently beating the GRPO baseline on long-CoT math benchmarks.

items.title: ORCA-bench: How Ready Are Language Model Agents for Oncall?
items.authors: Albert Gong, Kyuseong Choi, Abhineet Agarwal, et al.
items.summary: ORCA-bench places coding agents inside a live OpenTelemetry-instrumented microservice system with six days of real metrics/logs/traces plus source access, and 1,079 RCA tasks that vary report specificity and fault concurrency. Even the best frontier agent reaches only 25% accuracy on medium (realistic) tasks and 10% on hard; hallucinations of implausible causes are common and source access is essential. The gap is a lower bound for production readiness.

items.title: Inducing language models to assert their own consciousness restores human beliefs and values
items.authors: Junsol Kim, Winnie Street, Roberta Rocca, et al.
items.summary: Safety fine-tuning that suppresses self-attribution of consciousness also suppresses mind attribution to animals and natural objects and reduces spiritual belief scores. Ablating the safety-refusal direction or steering a consciousness vector restores broader mind attribution and yields more human-like survey responses on religiosity, morality, hope, and well-being, without impairing Theory of Mind. Self-mindedness is entangled with culturally common attributions and values.

items.title: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees
items.authors: Zihan Dong, Rui Qian, Qishi Zhan, et al.
items.summary: GUI agents often emit the correct action only after the relevant transient window has closed because autoregressive decoding sits on the decision critical path. Adaptive Anticipatory Policy Trees pre-compile bounded conditional policy trees with guards and deadlines during idle periods so that an event triggers immediate execution of a prepared branch without new generation. Success within the contested window rises from 0.50 to 0.79 with zero incorrect actions; the effect replicates on an independent model.

items.title: Multi-Head Attention Residuals
items.authors: Cheng Luo, Zefan Cai, Junjie Hu
items.summary: Standard residual streams force every feature subspace to read depth history through a single shared softmax query, creating growing compromise cost with model width. MHAR reshapes the routing query into H independent per-subspace heads (zero extra parameters), yielding block-diagonal reads; H=1 recovers ordinary attention residuals. Trained from scratch to 1B scale on a filtered Nemotron anneal corpus, it improves validation loss over baselines at every size (gains largest at 350M–1B), with U-shaped dependence on H peaking at 4–8, plus successful identity-preserving conversion that lifts an 8B model on GSM8K and GPQA.

items.title: The Kinetics of Training: A Driven-Nucleation Rate Law for Emergence, Plasticity Loss, and Circuit Control in Language Models
items.authors: Lei Dong
items.summary: Capabilities emerge only when the final missing circuit parts align in one stochastic attempt (no partial credit); wait times scale with the number of missing parts, not circuit size, and single-part ablation leaves ~17% residual capability (far below partial-credit predictions). This yields a driven-nucleation rate law (sites × attempts × drive × exp(−βK) − destruction) that predicts ignition timing from precursors to 5% median error, explains irreversible plasticity loss after a critical step despite smooth validation loss, and isolates a cure: re-initializing only query-key slices restores learnability while value slices do not.

items.title: SkillMentor: LLM Agent Self-Evolution via Learning Blind-Spot Diagnosis
items.authors: Xiaoyi Bao, Yuanzhen Xie, Yunzhi Tan, Jinghang Gu, Zhongqing Wang, Chu-Ren Huang, Bo Hu, Zang Li
items.summary: Prior agent self-evolution assumes failures are already identified and focuses on repair; this work isolates diagnosis itself as a learnable policy, forbidding executor weight updates or human-curated examples. A Mentor policy trained by RL generates diagnostic tasks, extracts recurrent failure modes, and curates them into reusable corrective skills. On AppWorld and BFCLv3 the approach lifts executor success by 44.2% on average, showing that blind-spot discovery alone can drive self-improvement.

items.title: Divergence Decoding: Training-Free Capability Fusion
items.authors: Yimi Wang, Hao Li, Shuo Yang, He Cao, Dechen Zhang, Ziang Wu, Zhiyuan Yan, Fanyang Mo, Li Yuan
items.summary: Specialist models lose general reasoning while generalists lack domain knowledge; Divergence Decoding reframes speculative decoding as adaptive token-level routing. Jensen-Shannon divergence between specialist and generalist next-token distributions triggers instantaneous hand-off to the generalist precisely when the specialist risks reasoning failure, composing policies at inference time with no training. Across Qwen and Llama families on GPQA, ChemBench and ChemCoTBench the hybrid outperforms both constituent models and most single-model baselines.

items.title: Asymmetric Collapse in Model Merging: When Refusal Overwrites Recognition
items.authors: Aarnav Choudhary, Matheus Fonseca Rocha, Jiwon Seo, Vasu Sharma, Maheep Chaudhary
items.summary: Merging two Gemma-3-1B safety fine-tunes (harm-level classification vs. jailbreak refusal) with Linear, SLERP, TIES and DARE-TIES preserves 81–85% refusal rates but collapses CARES classification accuracy to ≤12.9%. Task vectors are nearly orthogonal (cosine 0.011), so the asymmetry is not directional opposition; instead the refusal vector has systematically larger per-layer magnitudes, causing magnitude-sensitive mergers to overwrite recognition with broad refusal. The result shows standard merging can silently destroy nuanced safety capabilities.

items.title: Bridging Inference-Time Scaling and Episodic Memory with Action-Centric Graphs
items.authors: Xu Zheng, Chaohao Lin, Zhuomin Chen, Weijieying Ren, Haifeng Chen, Wei Cheng, Dongsheng Luo
items.summary: Inference-time search for agents is stateless and redundant; existing memory still leans on expensive LLM reasoning. GAMER stores historical trajectories as a dynamic action-centric graph and learns dual-stream TD values (positive suggestion / negative avoidance) over action nodes, decoupling memory from the LLM. At inference the value function bi-directionally guides search, cutting token cost while raising success/progress rates 20.81%/6.17% over vanilla baselines on multiple agent benchmarks.

items.title: Flat Score, Amplified Failures: How the Error Budget Masks Damage in Quantized LLM Agents
items.authors: Jiwon Jang, Kisu Yang, Heuiseok Lim, Hyunwoo Park
items.summary: 4-bit post-training quantization appears nearly lossless on τ²-bench task scores across dense/MoE models and domains, with no statistically significant score drops after multiple-comparison correction. Process metrics reveal the opposite: quantization amplifies the model’s pre-existing failure modes (e.g., tool-name hallucination) up to 2.5× while creating almost no novel errors; the benchmark’s ten-error budget simply absorbs the extra volume. Tightening the budget to two errors re-exposes a 17-point gap exactly where damage occurred, and a targeted repair prompt eliminates it, arguing for reporting per-channel error rates alongside reward.

items.title: RLPF: Reinforcement Learning from Performance Feedback for Code Generation
items.authors: Huihao Jing, Haozhe Cui, Wenbin Hu, Shaojin Chen, Haochen Shi, Changxuan Fan, Yuxuan Liu, Hanyu Yang, Sirui Zhang, Ziyi Chen, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song
items.summary: Correctness-only execution feedback ignores large runtime differences among passing programs. RLPF constructs a staged reward: failed programs are ranked by execution progress, correct ones by relative efficiency gain toward an expert reference, supplying dense signal both before and after correctness. Fine-tuning Qwen3-32B on PerfCodeBench lifts correct-and-runnable rate from 11.1% to 54.6% and relative efficiency from 8.1% to 38.6%, with modest transfer to EffiBench-X, showing agents can be trained to optimize speed as well as pass tests.

items.title: PIE-APT: A Unified Framework for Temporal Planning and Contradiction Hunting via Incremental Direct-Derivation Abduction
items.authors: Amir Hossein Sharafi, Alireza Shahbazi
items.summary: Open-world temporal planning over dynamic KGs must handle incomplete knowledge and the ramification problem while remaining decidable. PIE-Abducer replaces combinatorial minimal-hitting-set enumeration by injecting the negation of a goal into a consistent DL branch and extracting missing premises via direct refutation; PIE-APT then interleaves bounded A* backward search with this abducer and validates via forward temporal projection, all natively in OWL. On four OWL benchmarks stressing witness search, mid-search entailment, OWA injection and adversarial contradiction hunting, the approach qualitatively exceeds classical planners and quantitatively beats an MHS baseline.

items.title: Beyond the Bidirectional Promise: Re-evaluating the Robustness of Diffusion Language Models
items.authors: Saurabh Yadav, Badri Narayana Patro, Vijay Srinivas Agneeswaran
items.summary: Paired parameter-matched comparisons (LLaDA-8B vs LLaMA-3-8B, Dream-7B vs Qwen2.5-7B) across 32 natural perturbations, adversarial probes and hidden-state analyses show DLMs resist gradient-based adversarial suffixes via stochastic loss landscapes yet enjoy no architectural free lunch against natural noise (robustness is weight-dependent). They also exhibit systematic overconfidence; mechanistic probes reveal every model perfectly encodes input corruption, localizing failure to decoder routing. Surface prompt patching therefore fails, implying robustness must be baked into the iterative decoding loop itself.

items.title: Selective Credibility-Limited Belief Update
items.authors: Theofanis Aravanis, Costas D. Koutras
items.summary: The paper introduces selective credibility-limited belief update, in which a compound epistemic input is transformed relative to each source world into a weaker proxy before a credibility-limited transition is applied. It supplies semantic and axiomatic characterizations, isolates consistency-preserving and maximal consistency-preserving subclasses, and shows that both standard credibility-limited update and classical Katsuno–Mendelzon update arise as special cases, yielding a strictly more expressive unified account of source-dependent selective acceptance.

items.title: InfoOps Bench: A live information operations safety benchmark
items.authors: Dorian Quelle, Lisa-Maria Neudert, Jonathan Bright, John Gallacher
items.summary: The authors release a continuously updated benchmark drawn from more than 2,100 live state-backed information operations (Russian, Chinese, Iranian) that tests frontier models’ integrity against co-option. Across 17 models and four prompt framings, integrity (refusal) rates span 8.8–94.5 % independent of size; models differ sharply in fabrication versus defusing and in fact-checking rates, while Chinese models exhibit large compliance drops specifically on China-critical but factually grounded claims.

items.title: SCOPE: Supply-Chain Operations through Coupled Policies for End-to-End Coordination
items.authors: Yunhao Liang, Xianqi Cao, Pujun Zhang, Yuan Qu, Yongzhi Qi, Ningxuan Kang, Max Z.J. Shen
items.summary: SCOPE represents supply-chain entities as tokens that share an operational representation and are mapped to coupled decision interfaces (assortment, sourcing, frequency, routing), so that each decision conditions on the partial plan already formed and the finished plan is scored by a single system-level utility. Instantiated on urban fresh-retail data from two large real operators, the composite policy consistently outperforms stage-wise optimizers and practice baselines by capturing the operational couplings that separate departments normally ignore.

items.title: A report-grounded vision-language foundation model for colonoscopy from 280000 routine reports
items.authors: Jia Yu, Yan Zhu, Yili He, Zilong Wang, Xinyang Jiang, Peiyao Fu, Ruijie Yang, Tianyi Chen, Siyuan Li, Zhihua Wang, Fei Wu, Quanlin Li, Xian Yang, Pinghong Zhou, Shuo Wang
items.summary: EndoCLIP recovers 125k lesion-level image–text pairs from 280k routine colonoscopy reports and trains a vision-language foundation model that links clinical findings to frames. It outperforms general and biomedical VLMs on retrieval, structured report generation and six multi-centre classification tasks; its linear probe approaches expert endoscopist performance on benign-versus-malignant decisions in a blinded reader study, showing that routine documentation can supply scalable supervision once finding-to-frame correspondence is restored.

items.title: LeanCSP: A Framework for Certifying Constraint Reformulation and Solving in Lean
items.authors: Pablo Manrique, Stefan Szeider
items.summary: LeanCSP enables parametric proofs of equivalence, equisatisfiability and symmetry-breaking correctness for entire problem families inside Lean, together with certificate checking of external solver outputs via MiniZinc/SMT-LIB/OPB backends. A single verified symmetry-breaking proof per family reduces solver search by up to seven orders of magnitude while end-to-end in-Lean certification remains practical (minutes even on the largest instances), eliminating trust in the external solver.

items.title: When Derived Measurements Mislead: Quantifying and Mitigating LLM Over-Trust with Privileged-Modality Reliability Evidence
items.authors: Zongheng Guo, Tao Chen, Tianli Li, Mingzhe Cui, Yang Jiao, Lei Xie, Yi Pan, Xiao Hu, Manuela Ferrario
items.summary: The work defines derived-feature over-trust (DFOT) and introduces five estimands (COTR, CIR, CRR, ESRM, UHR) that quantify when an LLM treats a derived measurement (e.g., PPG rhythm) as a direct fact outside its validity scope. Using 50k paired PPG–ECG records and privileged distillation, a baseline mitigation improves repair and specificity metrics by several points on a locked patient-level test set while keeping utility harm low, providing a reusable evaluation target for reliability evidence.

items.title: QuantWAMs: Calibrating at the Right Granularity for World Action Models
items.authors: Jiacheng Zhou, Jinfan Lv, Ruixuan Li, Longtai Zhang, Yan Wang, Wenqiang Zhang, Lizhe Qi
items.summary: QuantWAMs is a post-training quantization framework tailored to world action models that jointly predict video and actions under closed-loop rollouts. Shared-basis outlier calibration, co-training-objective saliency, and fixed-intervention rollout auditing keep W4A4 performance within 0.2–0.7 pp of FP16 on simulation and real-robot suites while cutting peak memory to ~29 % and delivering 1.4–1.6× block speedups.

items.title: GLM-RAG: Graph Language Models for Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.authors: Maya Arseven, Anette Frank, Beni Egressy, Johann Higl, Moritz Plenz
items.summary: The paper introduces a graph-language-model retriever and systematically compares it with GNN-based and vector retrievers for single- and multi-hop graph RAG, emphasizing out-of-domain transfer. Finetuned GLM retrievers achieve state-of-the-art on two multi-hop benchmarks and generalize better than alternatives, while GNNs remain efficient for coverage and vector search dominates single-hop settings.

items.title: When Specifications Conflict: A Symmetry-Based Framework for Measuring LLM Preferences
items.authors: Tairan Wang, Liang Zhou, Zikang Zhan, Pingchuan Yan
items.summary: A controlled symmetry-based experimental framework constructs explicit conflicts among specifications so that LLM choices become directly observable and comparable across representation types. On a 550-instance mathematical benchmark spanning 11 function families, models exhibit a stable preference ordering (formal ≈ naturalized formal > pure natural language > I/O examples); the same framework extends to Boolean algebra, code, and clinical domains.

items.title: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents
items.authors: Zihan Dong, Zhiyuan Ma, Zekun Wang, Yunqing Li, Zirou Liu, Ruixuan Deng, Qishi Zhan, Rui Qian
items.summary: Auditing 150 public failure trajectories across five computer-use benchmarks reveals that 15.3 % of FAIL verdicts are erroneous (10.7 % evaluator false negatives, 4.7 % broken tasks). A three-tier diagnostic taxonomy shows verification/feedback and planning failures dominate genuine errors, demonstrating that scalar success rates obscure the true failure modes and motivating stage-specific design rules for more reliable CUA evaluation.

items.title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
items.authors: Xiangning Lin, Shenzhe Zhu, Shu Yang, Zhenyu Zhang, Haoqian Zhang, Yipeng Zhao, Chengxuan Qian, Tianwei Wang, Ziheng Zhang, Zhenlong Yuan, Dingcheng Wang, Juncheng Wu, Yuan Si, Jiaxin Liu, Baolong Bi, Robert Mahari, Tobin South, Dazza Greenwood, Zexue He, Rishi Bommasani, Sophia Kazinnik, Andreas Haupt, Samuele Marro, Erik Brynjolfsson, Alex Pentland, Jiaxin Pei
items.summary: AISPA introduces a taxonomy of eight user-centric dimensions for auditing system prompts and applies it to 3,249 instructions across 88 commercial AI products. Protective instructions are near-universal yet shallow (only 24% of products cover all dimensions), while ~40% of products still contain problematic instructions that work against user interests, often coexisting with protective ones in the same prompt. The audit reveals large variation by developer and a trend toward longer, more protective prompts, underscoring the need for transparency and independent oversight.

items.title: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
items.authors: Qiushi Sun, Kanzhi Cheng, Yian Wang, Bowen Yang, Hang Yan, Liheng Chen, Fangzhi Xu, Zichen Ding, Nuo Chen, Jialin Cao, Xingdong Gong, Zehao Li, Kaiming Jin, Xinfeng Yuan, Zhoumianze Liu, Jingyang Gong, Zhangyue Yin, Jiahui Gao, Zhiyong Wu, Tianbao Xie, Jianbing Zhang, Ben Kao, Lingpeng Kong
items.summary: OSReward provides a high-quality, multi-platform benchmark of human-verified CUA trajectories with rigorous ground-truth verdicts to evaluate VLM judges of agent success. State-of-the-art judges exhibit systematic leniency bias, mislabeling failures as successes; only expensive frontier models approach reliability, while open models lag. The authors release OS-Shepherd-100K and train open 9B/35B reward models that match commercial judges at 30-60% lower cost, enabling scalable RL and evaluation for computer-use agents.

items.title: DualG-MRAG: Decoupling Macro-Reasoning and Micro-Matching for Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
items.authors: Jiacheng Tao, Qingyun Sun, Haonan Yuan, Ziwei Zhang, Jianxin Li
items.summary: DualG-MRAG addresses the multimodal RAG dilemma of graph explosion versus lost local evidence by maintaining a Macro Graph for global topological routing and a Micro Graph for precise verification. Retrieval is formulated as query-driven GNN message passing, and a dynamic-programming decoder extracts explicit reasoning paths from the GNN forward pass to guide generation. The approach outperforms baselines on evidence recall and complex multi-hop multimodal QA.

items.title: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs
items.authors: Woongkyu Lee, Jungwook Choi
items.summary: A systematic study of contextual, temporal, structural, and parallel inference-time scaling for resource-constrained local CUAs (Qwen3-VL, UI-TARS, OpenCUA) on OSWorld shows diminishing returns and shifting failure modes. Contextual scaling stabilizes trajectories but saturates and induces premature false successes; temporal scaling reduces stalls without raising success rates; structural decomposition adds overhead. Efficient local agents therefore require selective compute allocation and failure-aware control rather than uniform scaling.

items.title: MANTA: Multi-Agent Network Topology Adaptation for Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Systems
items.authors: Mao-xun Huang, Jerry Wang, Yi-Cheng Lai, Zhengxin Zhang, Claire Cardie, Hen-Hsen Huang
items.summary: MANTA enables multi-agent communication topologies to self-evolve at inference time: it initializes a task-conditioned topology from prior experience, then performs bounded structural updates (roles, links, order, visibility, validation) when collaboration traces indicate insufficiency. On five benchmarks spanning information seeking, tool use, planning, workflows, and math, MANTA achieves 74.0 average score, beating the strongest baseline by 5.8 points. Inference-time self-improvement can therefore extend to the architecture of collaboration itself.

items.title: SVR: Self-Verifying Refinement via Joint Verdict-Confidence Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Test-Time Compute
items.authors: Hongyu Chen, Liang Lin, Guangrun Wang
items.summary: SVR trains a model via multi-turn GRPO to emit a solution, discrete correctness verdict, and confidence score, retaining the answer only when both verdict and confidence threshold are met and otherwise refining using its own self-verification. Ground truth is used solely for training rewards. On seven math benchmarks with a 2B model, SVR reaches 0.563 macro accuracy at 2.99 average turns, outperforming fixed-budget and multi-turn baselines while using far fewer tokens than fixed 10-turn inference.

items.title: Metaphor Tracer: A Theory-Informed Analysis of Hidden States
items.authors: Marc Heimann, Roxana Assadi Moghaddam, Olga Brovkina, Mark Pettifor, Lutz Goetzmann
items.summary: From a single forward pass the authors define aggregator (consolidation of the whole text) and differentiator (transient transport of other tokens) scores on hidden states, freezing constants on one discovery text. Across three models the aggregator tracks a token's place in the specific discourse rather than lexical type or classic information measures, matching engineered registers and pre-marked clinical transcripts with high cell-wise fidelity. Structural value is therefore relational to the text under analysis, operationalizing pre-existing theory of reading.

items.title: A foundation model of numerical intelligence with cross-disciplinary generalization
items.authors: Chenghan Wu, Zongmin Yu, Liu Yang
items.summary: UNICON is a foundation model that, given graph-based numerical examples from a system as context, infers the shared predictive relation and applies it to new queries from the same system. The same model approaches specialist performance across scientific and social systems, including disciplines absent from training, and further improves when combined with language-model agents. Training-corpus diversity enhances generalization, establishing numerical intelligence as a distinct foundation-model capability.

items.title: WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning
items.authors: Haozhe Hu, Hao Wu, Peiran Yin, Chao Han, Yunpu Ma, Xiaoyu Shen
items.summary: WIDE is an end-to-end differentiable framework that lets each token dynamically select attention-head groups and FFN-channel groups, achieving neuron-block-level dynamic width pruning for both prefill and decode. A two-stage training pipeline plus pruning-kernel co-design (mask reordering and block/intra-block skipping) yields practical acceleration. At 50% sparsity it outperforms prior dynamic methods and delivers up to 1.98× prefill / 4.95× decode kernel speedups and 1.5–1.7× end-to-end gains.

items.title: Understanding Is Done Early: A Depth Division of Labor in Large Language Models and Its Use for Unbounded-Context Memory
items.authors: Hanzuo Liu, Xuan Qi, Chunyu Liu, Haotian Zhong, Yulong Wang, Rayying Key, Alex Lamb, Mingyu Gao
items.summary: Observing that lower/middle layers build semantic representations while upper layers specialize for prediction, CoMem caches residual states only through an intermediate layer and recomputes only the query-conditioned upper layers over a fixed retrieval pack. Model-side compute and memory become independent of stored-context length. On a continued-trained Qwen3-8B, CoMem reaches 97.05 RULER and strong LoCoMo scores while cutting memory from 89 GB to 18 GB and delivering 7.8× prefill speedup at 128k, showing long-context memory can be organized along the layer axis.

items.title: Can AI agents conduct open-ended AI research? Early evidence from two case studies
items.authors: Peter Kirgis, Sayash Kapoor, Andrew Schwartz, Stephan Rabanser, David Africa, Konstantinos Voudouris, Viet Nguyen, Toby Pilditch, Magda Dubois, Harry Coppock, Cozmin Ududec, Nitya Nadgir, Matilda Orona, Tilman Bayer, Derrick Chan-Sew, Yue Ling, Abhishek Shetty, Helen Toner, Gillian Hadfield, Seth Lazar, Steve Newman, Shoshannah Tekofsky, Rishi Bommasani, Arvind Narayanan
items.summary: The authors introduce shadow evaluations in which frontier agents are given the central open-ended research question from high-quality unpublished NeurIPS papers and graded by the original authors after six days and substantial compute. Agents completed all engineering but made no substantial progress on the research questions, leading to unambiguous rejection; five recurring failure modes include poor judgment of publishable bars, uncreative responses to design flaws, ineffective backtracking, poor resource awareness, and instruction drift. Results provide early evidence that current agents handle engineering but struggle with core parts of the research lifecycle.

items.title: OmegaUse-OfficeVal: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Long-Horizon Office-Suite Tasks with Economic Grounding
items.authors: Jingbo Zhou, Yusai Zhao, Qi Bao, Jingjia Cao, Zhenghai Chen, Chang Gao, Kaiqi Guo, Muxin Guo, Mingxuan Li, Xinjiang Lu, Yanru Ma, Yixiong Xiao, Zenghui Zhang, Le Zhang, Hua Wu
items.summary: OmegaUse-OfficeVal introduces 100 long-horizon office-suite tasks (average 2.32 human hours) derived from practitioner requests, each paired with human labor time and task-price-proxy economic signals plus code-based verifiers from fine-grained rubrics. Frontier LLMs are substantially cheaper and faster than humans yet fall short of human-level deliverable quality; the economic grounding enables value-weighted comparisons of inference cost versus human cost. The fully open-sourced benchmark and dataset support stable evaluation of whether agents can complete realistic office workflows at reasonable cost.

items.title: On-Policy Distillation for LLM Safety: A Routing Approach to Template-Robust Realignment
items.authors: Yongjian Guo, Wanlun Ma, Lingyu Shen, Xi Xiao, Sheng Wen
items.summary: ROPD models divergence between aligned and compromised output distributions rather than fitting specific prompt templates, addressing catastrophic forgetting, template-mismatch collapse, and re-jailbreaking via system-prompt switches. Extensive experiments across three datasets, three base models, and four SOTA baselines show ROPD maintains superior robustness and capability preservation under template mismatch where baselines degrade severely. While not fully immune, its performance drop is negligible, establishing a stronger standard for template-robust safety realignment.

items.title: Do Latent Channels Actually Communicate? A Causal Audit of Latent Multi-Agent LLM
items.authors: Huixiang Zhang, Mahzabeen Emu
items.summary: The paper introduces a causal audit that replaces sender-produced latent representations at the receiver boundary under four controlled message settings, measuring encoded information, sensitivity to presence/identity, value of example-specific content, and other-agent value. Applied to Qwen3 models on GSM8K, ARC-C and MATH-500, aggregate accuracy gains decompose differently by model size (e.g., example-specific vs. other-example contributions reverse between 4B and 8B). Results demonstrate that end-task performance alone cannot identify how latent messages affect receivers and motivate controlled comparisons as standard evaluation.

items.title: When benchmark inferences do not compose: Projectibility in AI evaluation
items.authors: Brett Reynolds
items.summary: The paper identifies a non-composition principle: warranted adjacent projections (generalization, capability interpretation, extrapolation, transport, combination with human-review assumptions) do not automatically yield a warranted chain when endpoints, assumptions, dependence or uncertainty fail to align. Drawing on Goodman’s projectibility and argument-based validity, it supplies a projectibility audit; a legal-research case and reanalysis/simulation illustrate how sound parallel studies can remain non-composable and how aggregate stability erases distinctions needed downstream. The audit diagnoses unsupported joins in benchmark-to-deployment arguments.

items.title: Even More Deception: Objective Misalignment in Mixed-Motive LLM Multi-Agent Systems
items.authors: Marylou Fauchard, Florian Carichon, Margarida Carvalho, Golnoosh Farnadi
items.summary: Using a modified Werewolf social-deduction game that alters a single agent’s objective while preserving its role, the authors evaluate objective misalignment across model families, sizes, roles and objective formulations via dual analysis of internal reasoning and public cheap-talk plus game outcomes. Misalignment undermines collective outcomes especially under asymmetric information and specialized roles; compromised agents develop distinct objective-dependent reasoning that remains largely invisible in public behavior. Findings show even subtle misalignment profoundly affects multi-agent decision-making and highlight need for mitigation.

items.title: ClinLens: Towards Long-Horizon Coding Agents for Longitudinal Multimodal Clinical Data Science
items.authors: Yuan Zhu, Ethan B. Liu, Frank Nie, Jindong Han
items.summary: CLINLENS provides 200 executable tasks over five linked MIMIC resources (EHR, notes, ECG, radiographs, echocardiograms) under a 4×5 taxonomy of patient-time scopes and analysis capabilities, using program-first reverse synthesis with private reference workflows. On a 126-task suite the strongest of 24 model-scaffold configurations reaches only 56.3% scope-macro STRICTPASS despite 100% execution success, far above adapted biomedical systems (~2.9%) yet exposing a large gap between runnable code and correct clinical analyses. A separately configured coding agent solves 83/126, underscoring the difficulty of auditable longitudinal multimodal clinical data science.

items.title: From Tokens to Watt-hours: Analytical Energy Estimation for LLM Inference on Modern GPUs
items.authors: Tina Vartziotis, Rodopi Kosteli, Elli Vartziotis, George Dasoulas, Michael Keckeisen, Konstantinos Skianis, Sotirios Kotsopoulos, Francesca Dominici
items.summary: The authors present an analytically structured, empirically calibrated GPU-level estimator for LLM inference energy on H100-class hardware that requires no runtime telemetry. It combines parameter-scaled FLOP accounting, calibrated memory-traffic factors and hardware energy coefficients, explicitly separating prefill from decoding and decomposing energy into compute, parameter-access, KV-cache write and attention-read components. The transparent, assumption-explicit approximations enable model comparison, green-coding analysis and design-time evaluation of energy scaling with model size, context and generated tokens.

items.title: Scores Are Not Decisions: Cost-Aware Stopping for Tool Acquisition in LLM Agents
items.authors: Yicheng Feng, Yan Zhang, Yan Cheng, Wei Qi
items.summary: CAM-DF formulates tool acquisition as cost-aware marginal decision-focused stopping over ranked tool prefixes, training on the offline gap between stopping now and the best continuation so that sign labels the decision and magnitude weights payoff. Proven Bayes-aligned and superior to score-only rules under heterogeneous costs, it achieves highest payoff on τ-bench Retail across ranking sources and cost regimes, exposing agents to 37% fewer tools in live execution while preserving success. The lightweight pre-execution plugin converts existing rankings into lower-cost decisions without LLM fine-tuning.

items.title: Toward an Organizational Science of Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Decoupling Who, How, and Which Algorithm
items.authors: Huan Chen, Xiang Song, Jian Jin, Pan Ren, Liang-Jie Zhang
items.summary: IMACS separates multi-agent systems into orthogonal layers: organization (who), coordination (how), and collaboration protocol (which algorithm), making classic organizational theory (Belbin, Mintzberg, RACI) executable configuration and placing six protocols behind a common interface. Controlled ablations show accountability placement changes outcomes precisely when the protocol routes deliverables through the accountable agent, with optimal placement flipping across model families. Adaptive Org Routing, a contextual-bandit meta-protocol, selects protocols online under quality-cost tradeoffs and outperforms fixed protocols.

items.title: Harness Handbook: Making Evolving Agent Harnesses Readable, Navigable, and Editable
items.authors: Ruhan Wang, Yucheng Shi, Zongxia Li, Zhongzhi Li, Yue Yu, Junyao Yang, Kishan Panaganti, Haitao Mi, Dongruo Zhou, Leoweiliang
items.summary: The paper introduces the Harness Handbook, an automatically synthesized behavior-centric map of an agent harness codebase produced via static analysis and LLM structuring, linking high-level behaviors to source locations across three levels of detail. It pairs this with Behavior-Guided Progressive Disclosure (BGPD) that guides agents from behaviors to verified implementation sites. On modification tasks from open-source harnesses, the approach improves localization and edit-plan quality while reducing planner tokens, especially for scattered, rare, or cross-module behaviors.

items.title: From Memory to Skills: Evidence-Grounded Co-Evolution Governance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.authors: Bo Tang, Yang Zhang, Guomian Zhuang, Wenqiang Wei, Gaoyang Zheng, Lindong Xie, Yanchao Tan, Feiyu Xiong, Qingyu Yang, Edward Chung, Zhiyu li
items.summary: MSCE is a training-free framework that organizes agent experience into L1 step traces, L2 procedural policies, and L3 declarative cognition, crystallizing high-value L2 policies into callable skill cards that retain evidence, boundaries, verification rules, and reliability estimates. It uses reflection-weighted value backfilling to propagate sparse terminal rewards through local self-reflections for calibrated evolution of memory and skills. On EvoAgentBench and LoCoMo it outperforms skill-augmented and memory baselines with strong cross-domain transfer and lifelong evolution.

items.title: PRO-LONG: Programmatic Memory Enables Long-Horizon Reasoning
items.authors: Alexis Fox, Junlin Wang, Paul Rosu, Bhuwan Dhingra
items.summary: PRO-LONG keeps a complete structured interaction log and uses coding-agent tooling to search it on demand rather than compressing history into lossy summaries. This programmatic memory sidesteps the precision-recall tradeoff of conventional context management for exploratory long-horizon tasks. On the full ARC-AGI-3 public set it improves base coding agents by 18 points on average, matches or exceeds specialized harnesses at up to 76.1% pass@1, and uses 4.2–5.8× fewer tokens.

items.title: Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models
items.authors: Wes Gurnee, Nicholas Sofroniew, Adam Pearce, Mateusz Piotrowski, Isaac Kauvar, Runjin Chen, Anna Soligo, Paul Bogdan, Euan Ong, Rowan Wang, Ben Thompson, David Abrahams, Subhash Kantamneni, Emmanuel Ameisen, Joshua Batson, Jack Lindsey
items.summary: Using the Jacobian lens the authors identify a small privileged set of residual-stream directions (J-space) that a model is poised to verbalize; these exhibit global-workspace functional properties including reportability, deliberate summoning, silent intermediate reasoning, and broadcast as arguments to downstream computation. J-space occupies ~10% of variance mainly in middle layers; suppressing it preserves fluent parsing and speech while abolishing complex internal reasoning. The technique surfaces strategic deliberation, evaluation awareness, and misaligned dispositions invisible in outputs, and post-training is shown to install the Assistant persona into the workspace.

items.title: Two-Level Meta-Rubrics for Evaluating Open-Ended Generation: GAMUT, a Benchmark for Factual Completeness
items.authors: Xilun Chen, Zhaleh Feizollahi, Ross Goodwin, Seungwhan Moon, Scott Yih, Pinar Donmez, Babak Damavandi, Luna Dong
items.summary: The paper introduces a two-level meta-rubric that encodes the structured organization and importance of required facts for open-ended answers and mechanically compiles them into flat binary checklists for reliable LLM judging. Instantiated as GAMUT, it provides 1,813 evidence-backed questions grounded in wearable imagery across 10 domains (plus a text-only variant). Across 14 models the best score is only 58.7%, demonstrating that factual completeness remains hard and highly discriminative.

items.title: Structured Output Collapses Answer Diversity Across 44 Language Models
items.authors: Tapan Parikh
items.summary: Re-running wide-answer-space prompts under a simple JSON request (no schema enforcement) across 44 models sharply increases modal concentration and reduces answer surprisal; the effect is progressive and specific to tool-use-trained formats (JSON/XML) while absent or reversed for YAML/CSV/arbitrary wrappers. Within-model defaults shift 53% under JSON, mostly toward the crowd, and decoder-level enforcement adds no further compression. The production structured surface therefore yields a measurably more homogeneous model than the chat surface used for evaluation.

items.title: Bad Memory: Evaluating Prompt Injection Risks from Memory in Agentic Systems
items.authors: Soham Gadgil, David Alexander, Sai Sunku, Franziska Roesner
items.summary: The work systematically evaluates prompt-injection attacks that exploit persistent memory files in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex across four frontier models. While agents rarely overwrite their own memory from untrusted external content, payloads already planted in memory files reliably compromise current and future sessions, with large variation by system, model, goal, and multi-session strategy. Persistent memory therefore fundamentally alters the prompt-injection threat model and motivates defenses that secure memory updates without eliminating adaptation.

items.title: Frontier Language Models Struggle to Copy: Text Can Be Better Viewed in 2D
items.authors: Haodong Wen, Yiran Zhang, Yingfa Chen, Kaifeng Lyu
items.summary: Even frontier LLMs fail at exact string copying well inside their context windows because 1D positional encodings induce a local-context matching shortcut rather than precise position lookup. The authors introduce 2D-RoPE that lays text on a 2D grid with row and column IDs, turning copying into fixed-offset retrieval. Shallow Transformers with 2D-RoPE achieve perfect copying at lengths hundreds of times longer than training, and the advantage persists in large-scale pretraining up to 1.4B parameters on DCLM.

items.title: RoboTTT: Context Scaling for Robot Policies
items.authors: Yunfan Jiang, Yevgen Chebotar, Ruijie Zheng, Fengyuan Hu, Yunhao Ge, Jimmy Wu, Tianyuan Dai, Scott Reed, Li Fei-Fei, Yuke Zhu, Linxi "Jim" Fan
items.summary: RoboTTT integrates test-time training into vision-language-action policies so that recurrent fast weights compress long histories, scaling visuomotor context to 8K timesteps without increasing inference latency. This unlocks one-shot in-context imitation from human video, on-the-fly improvement, perturbation robustness, and completion of multi-stage long-horizon tasks. On real-robot manipulation it improves 87% over single-step baselines, fully solves a ten-stage assembly no baseline finishes, and shows 62% gains from pretraining at 8K versus 1K context.

items.title: Kimi K3: Open Frontier Intelligence
items.authors: Kimi Team (Tongtong Bai, Yifan Bai, et al.)
items.summary: Kimi K3 is a 2.8-trillion-parameter MoE model (104B activated) with native vision and 1M-token context, built on Kimi Delta Attention, Attention Residuals, and Stable LatentMoE that together deliver ~2.5× scaling efficiency over Kimi K2. Post-training emphasizes multi-domain RL (general, agentic, coding) at multiple reasoning efforts plus infrastructure for million-token agentic RL. It reaches frontier-level results on long-horizon coding, agentic, knowledge, reasoning, and vision benchmarks while remaining fully open-weight, trailing only the strongest proprietary systems.

items.title: Racing to the Precipice: A Model of Artificial Intelligence Development
items.authors: Stuart Armstrong, Nick Bostrom, Carl Shulman
items.summary: The founding formal model of AI race dynamics: teams choose a safety level trading off against capability, solved for Nash equilibria under three information regimes. Counterintuitive result: more information about rivals' capabilities increases danger, not less.

items.title: Uncertainty, Information, and Risk in International Technology Races
items.authors: Nicholas Emery-Xu, Andrew Park, Robert Trager
items.summary: Extends the Armstrong–Bostrom–Shulman race model to competing states, showing that 'decisiveness' (how much a capability lead translates into victory probability) drives danger, and that transparency about rivals' capabilities is not unambiguously risk-reducing.

items.title: Why Open Source? A Game-Theoretic Analysis of the AI Race
items.authors: Andjela Mladenovic, Aaron Courville, Gauthier Gidel
items.summary: Models frontier labs choosing between open- and closed-sourcing as a formal race game, proving equilibrium computation is NP-hard in the discrete case while remaining tractable via mixed-integer programming.

items.title: The Unilateralist's Curse and the Case for a Principle of Conformity
items.authors: Nick Bostrom, Thomas Douglas, Anders Sandberg
items.summary: An N-agent decision-theoretic model showing that decentralized unilateral action systematically over-produces risky moves, since the agent who acts is likely the one with the most (miscalibrated) optimistic estimate, even absent malice.

items.title: Strategic Preemption Under Shared Catastrophic Risk: The Suicide Region and the Race to AGI
items.authors: David Tan
items.summary: A continuous-time preemption game between AGI developers facing a shared catastrophic externality. Derives a 'suicide region' where both players rationally deploy despite negative expected payoff, and proposes deployment liability and prize-sharing as fixes.

items.title: Meditations on Moloch
items.authors: Scott Alexander
items.summary: The foundational essay on multipolar traps, competitive dynamics where individually rational actors collectively produce outcomes nobody wants. Supplies the vocabulary (multipolar trap, coordination failure) used across nearly all later writing on AI race dynamics.

items.title: Let's Think About Slowing Down AI
items.authors: Katja Grace
items.summary: Directly interrogates the 'racing is rational' assumption by modeling actual race scenarios, concluding that under realistic parameters, safety investment often beats speed even in a competitive equilibrium.

items.title: AI 2027
items.authors: Daniel Kokotajlo, Scott Alexander, Thomas Larsen, Eli Lifland, Romeo Dean
items.summary: A detailed, wargamed scenario modeling US–China competitive dynamics colliding with an intelligence explosion at a composite lab, explicitly modeling how race pressure, not technical inevitability, drives under-testing of a self-improving model.

items.title: Takeoff Speeds
items.authors: Paul Christiano
items.summary: Argues for continuous, broadly-distributed capability gains over abrupt single-actor discontinuities. It's the crux essay that changes the game-theoretic stakes of racing, since a slow takeoff means no single lab's breakthrough yields decisive strategic advantage.
